answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency scoring. Each identity’s actions are hashed per epoch and compared against its own prior pattern; a divergence beyond the umber threshold freezes its rewards until a fresh vertex of verified history rebuilds the score. Because maintaining many identities requires each to sustain a distinct, stable trajectory across epochs, an attacker pays the full operational cost of parallel consistent histories rather than a one-time fee. A single comet of anomalous activity collapses the whole cluster’s score, forcing costly rebuilds.
